name: Steve Novick

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Novick says he would make cost-effective, evidence-based investments in fighting homelessness.
positions.excerpt: make cost-effective evidence-based investments in fighting homelessness

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Novick says he supports greater PCEF investment in transportation, which the site calls the largest contributor to climate change.
positions.excerpt: Steve supports greater PCEF investment in the largest contributor to climate change - transportation.

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Novick proposes using PCEF money to offset water rate increases by paying part of the cost of the water filtration plant.
positions.excerpt: use PCEF to help offset water rate increases by paying part of the cost of the water filtration plant.

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Novick says that in response to blocked rail crossings the city should insist on an overcrossing.
positions.excerpt: We should insist on an overcrossing.

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Novick lists improving the permitting system and cleaning up the city as steps to draw housing investment.
positions.excerpt: improving the permitting system and cleaning up the city

positions.statement: In a September 2024 Willamette Week candidate interview, Novick said addiction treatment needs to be more widely available.
positions.excerpt: We need to have addiction treatment more widely available.

positions.statement: In a September 2024 Willamette Week candidate interview, Novick spoke of getting people off the street and into humane shelter such as tiny house villages.
positions.excerpt: getting folks off the street and into humane forms of shelter, like the tiny house villages

positions.statement: In a September 2024 Willamette Week candidate interview, Novick said electric utilities and transportation are a huge expense for low-income people.
positions.excerpt: electric utilities and transportation are a huge expense for low-income people

positions.statement: In an August 2026 City of Portland announcement, Novick is quoted saying Portland should help ensure Newport has the legal resources to fight ICE; he and the mayor each contributed $10,000.
positions.excerpt: we should help to make sure Newport has the legal resources it needs to fight ICE,

positions.statement: Willamette Week's October 2026 endorsement credits Novick with helping reverse a council effort to cut funding to Portland Children's Levy recipients.
positions.excerpt: Without Novick's moral pressure, the council would not have reversed an embarrassing effort to abruptly strip funding

voting_record.statement: Novick co-sponsored the ordinance to reinstate Portland's Fair Wages Ordinance, which the City Council passed unanimously, per a May 2025 City of Portland news release.
voting_record.excerpt: the Portland City Council voted unanimously today to reinstate the Fair Wages Ordinance
